key_idea: Build a two-column triangular algebra over a symmetric algebra and take the cone of two induced totally acyclic complexes, so that a bimodule map v whose comparison maps δ^a are isomorphisms in positive degrees cancels every positive self-extension of the resulting module.
reason: The triangular conversion principle (Proposition 2) is clean and explains the result conceptually: positive Ext vanishes because a long exact sequence is cancelled by the isomorphisms δ^a. Producing the input data, however, takes a hand-built 10-dimensional algebra with multiplication tables, an explicit Hochschild cocycle checked in an appendix, bar-resolution homotopies, and twisted-bimodule eigenvalue calculations, so the reason the counterexample exists is buried under heavy computation.
